subject: Commit acceleration incentive & reseller cascade mechanics
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@meridianhealth.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@meridianhealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace offer — need clarity on commit acceleration and reseller cascade

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We finished our internal review and Procurement wants to understand one structural piece before we move forward with a private offer. Two quick asks: 

1) Commit acceleration incentive: Meridian is willing to accelerate 12 months of usage into the first 6 months if there is an up-front benefit. What would Redwood be willing to provide in return (list price credit vs. one-time rebate vs. expanded seat count)? We need the economics mapped to our expected usage profile (attached table).

2) Reseller cascade: We work through a regional distributor (Cobalt Systems). How should the reseller commission / passback be handled inside the private offer waterfall so our distributor still gets paid on the accelerated portion without breaking the marketplace invoicing?

Attached: meridian_commit_table.xlsx (expected monthly consumption by sku)

Can you point us to a proposed flow or an example PO language? We want to avoid manual crediting after the term starts.

Best,
Alex

Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Partnerships
Meridian Health Tech
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@meridianhealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace offer — need clarity on commit acceleration and reseller cascade

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear asks and the table, this is helpful. High level answers below; I can send a short PO draft tomorrow that captures the waterfall.

1) Commit acceleration incentive: we usually offer a blend of two levers for acceleration: a one-time up-front credit (applied to the first invoice) + a volume-tier uplift that reduces unit price for the accelerated tranche. For your numbers, preliminary option: 8% up-front credit on the accelerated dollars + a 6% permanent unit discount on the accelerated SKUs for the first 12 months (applies only to the accelerated consumption). This keeps the marketplace list price consistent while giving Meridian an immediate benefit.

2) Reseller cascade: recommended flow is to include the distributor commission as a separate pass-through line in the private-offer waterfall. Marketplace invoices still go to Meridian; Redwood issues a consolidated commission settlement to Cobalt monthly based on the accelerated portion using a signed reseller annex. That avoids changing the public list price and keeps invoice routing simple.

I'll loop in Ben and Tessa internally to confirm margin math and whether we need a temporary escrow clause. Expect a PO draft + margin workback by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: proposed-po-draft.pdf (working draft)

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Principal Partner Manager | Redwood Inference

Ben / Tessa — forwarding Meridian's note and my reply. Key points to confirm:

- Proposed economics: 8% one-time credit (accelerated dollars) + 6% temporary unit price uplift for 12 months on accelerated skus. Is that acceptable from margin perspective for a reseller pass-through?
- Distributor (Cobalt) needs to keep commission on accelerated portion. Proposed operational flow: Meridian pays list price to AWS marketplace; Redwood separately settles commission to Cobalt monthly. Do we need an escrow holdback for the first 3 months to protect against overclaiming?

Can you review the attached spreadsheet and do a quick margin workback (include estimated infra cost delta for burst in first 6 months)? I'll include your numbers in the PO draft.

Camila

Alex — thanks for the patience. Per our internal check:

- Confirmed structure: 8% one-time credit applied to first invoice + a 6% unit discount applied to accelerated SKUs for months 1–12.
- Reseller cascade: we'll execute a reseller annex that defines Cobalt's commission at 9% on the accelerated dollars; Redwood will settle monthly against actual consumption. No change to the AWS/GCP list price — commission is a Redwood-to-distributor settlement outside of the marketplace invoice.
- Escrow: we recommend a 3-month reconciliation holdback of 2% to cover early churn/over-accelerations. At month 4, we reconcile actual usage vs. accelerated commitment and release/adjust the holdback.

Next steps: I attached a PO draft and a short waterfall table showing example invoices and the commission settlement. If that looks good, I can share a DocuSign link for Meridian's PO + the reseller annex.

DocuSign (sample): https://docusign.com/samples/meridian-po-2027
